bib.title: RankZephyr: Effective and Robust Zero-Shot Listwise Reranking is a Breeze!

question: Can a 7B open-source LLM distilled from RankGPT3.5 and RankGPT4 match or beat RankGPT4 as a zero-shot listwise reranker, and which training and inference choices matter?
hypothesis: An open 7B model can close the gap with proprietary RankGPT4 given strategic distillation choices (teacher, hard-negative source, variable windows, shuffled inputs).
contributions: RankZephyr, an open-source 7B listwise reranker (Zephyr-beta) matching or occasionally exceeding RankGPT4
Ablations on teacher, query selection, ADA2 vs BM25 training orderings, variable window sizes, first-stage retriever, shuffled input

method.summary: Zephyr-beta 7B is fine-tuned in two stages with instruction distillation of listwise permutations: first on RankGPT3.5 reorderings of BM25 top-20 for 100K MS MARCO queries, then on RankGPT4 reorderings of ADA2 top-20 for 5K random queries with random sub-window augmentation. Inference slides a window of 20 stride 10 over the top 100 candidates, optionally three times.

datasets.name: MS MARCO v1 training queries (RankGPT3.5 lists from Sun et al. 2023)
datasets.source: MS MARCO v1; lists provided by Sun et al. (2023)
datasets.preprocessing: malformed generations removed; shuffled input orders added alongside original BM25 orderings

datasets.name: RankGPT4 teacher data
datasets.size: no more than 5K queries (full model uses 5K random; ablations 1K or 2K)
datasets.preprocessing: ADA2 top-20 orderings as input; 3 random subsets of p<=20 passages sampled per list for variable windows

datasets.name: TREC DL19, DL20 (MS MARCO v1 passage, ~8.8M passages)
datasets.preprocessing: [n] in passages replaced by (n); ftfy fix_text applied

datasets.name: TREC DL21, DL22 (MS MARCO v2 passage, ~138M passages)
NovelEval-2306
datasets.size: 21 questions, four domains, top 20 Google Search candidates judged 0-2

models.name: RankZephyr
models.init_from: Zephyr-beta (Tunstall et al. 2023), built on Mistral 7B

other.note: described as rumored to be over two orders of magnitude larger

training.objective: instruction fine-tuning (distillation of teacher permutation outputs)
training.wall_clock: approximately 40 hours (stage 1); stage 2 about a tenth of the effort

other.stage2: started from stage-1 model; epochs, lr, batch size not stated

inference.decoding: deterministic (same input gives same output); decoding settings not given
inference.samples: RankZephyr one run; RankGPT3.5 averaged over six runs, RankGPT4 over three; shuffle experiments six shuffled orderings with 99% CI
inference.prompting: zero-shot RankLLM listwise prompt (Fig 1), no few-shot
inference.retrieval: first stage BM25, SPLADE++ ED, RepLLaMA or ADA2; top 100 (or 20); sliding window 20 stride 10

metrics.name: nDCG@10
metrics.definition: normalized discounted cumulative gain at cutoff 10

metrics.name: Judged@10
metrics.definition: share of top 10 with relevance judgments

eval.protocol: no significance tests except 99% CI in Table 7; GPT models averaged over repeated runs because non-deterministic

availability.weights: model checkpoints stated as shared; no URL given

prompts.text: <|system|> You are RankLLM, an intelligent assistant that can rank passages based on their relevancy to the query. <|user|> I will provide you with {num} passages, each indicated by a numerical identifier []. Rank the passages based on their relevance to the search query: {query}. [1] {passage 1} [2] {passage 2} ... [{num}] {passage {num}} Search Query: {query}. Rank the {num} passages above based on their relevance to the search query. All the passages should be included and listed using identifiers, in descending order of relevance. The output format should be [] > [], e.g., [4] > [2]. Only respond with the ranking results, do not say any word or explain. <|assistant|>

results.setup: MS MARCO v1 DL19/DL20, SPLADE++ ED top-100 candidates, sliding window 20/stride 10, full RankZephyr (Zephyr-beta 7B, GPT3.5 then GPT4 distillation); RankGPT4 (gpt-4) averaged over 3 runs

results.claim: RankZephyr beats RankGPT4 on DL20 reranking SPLADE++ ED top 100
results.setup: MS MARCO v1 DL19/DL20, SPLADE++ ED top-100 candidates, sliding window 20/stride 10, full RankZephyr (Zephyr-beta 7B, GPT3.5 then GPT4 distillation); RankGPT4 (gpt-4) averaged over 3 runs

results.claim: Three progressive passes (RankZephyr-rho) give the best DL19 and DL20 scores
results.setup: MS MARCO v1 DL19/DL20, SPLADE++ ED top-100 candidates, sliding window 20/stride 10, full RankZephyr (Zephyr-beta 7B, GPT3.5 then GPT4 distillation); RankGPT4 (gpt-4) averaged over 3 runs; three sequential sliding passes
results.table: Table 1, row (8) RankZephyr-rho, columns DL19, DL20

results.claim: On DL22 (MS MARCO v2) RankZephyr trails RankGPT4 when reranking SPLADE++ ED top 100
results.setup: MS MARCO v2 DL22, SPLADE++ ED top-100, window 20/10, out of domain

results.claim: On DL21 it also trails RankGPT4 with SPLADE++ ED
results.setup: MS MARCO v2 DL21, SPLADE++ ED top-100

results.claim: With BM25 as first stage (lower-quality candidates) RankZephyr beats RankGPT4 on DL22
results.setup: MS MARCO v2 DL22, BM25 top-100, window 20/10
results.note: Authors: rho beats RankGPT4 in three of four tasks with BM25; DL21 and COVID RankGPT4 higher for plain RankZephyr

results.claim: Shuffled SPLADE++ ED input costs RankZephyr 0.0146 nDCG@10 on DL19 (0.7816 to 0.7670) but RankGPT3.5 0.1476 (0.7504 to 0.6028)
results.setup: DL19, SPLADE++ ED top-100, mean over six shuffled orderings with 99% CI; RankGPT3.5 = gpt-3.5-turbo; deltas are our arithmetic from the table
results.note: With BM25 as first stage the drop is 0.7420 to 0.7378 (RankZephyr) and 0.6855 to 0.6158 (RankGPT3.5), i.e. 0.004 vs 0.070
results.table: Table 7, row (2d) Shuf. SPLADE++ ED, column DL19 nDCG@10
Table 7, row (1d) RankGPT3.5 Shuf. SPLADE++ ED, column DL19 nDCG@10

results.claim: On NovelEval-2306 RankZephyr has the best nDCG@1
results.setup: NovelEval-2306: 21 queries, Google Search top 20, single window, no progressive reranking
results.note: RankGPT4 is higher on nDCG@5 (0.8749 vs 0.8615) and nDCG@10 (0.9045 vs 0.8934)

results.claim: Variable-window training makes RankZephyr emit well-formed output at window 2/1 and 10/5
results.setup: BM25 top-100, single run (deterministic); RankGPT4 averaged over three runs

results.claim: A better first stage gives better reranking; gains shrink on stronger candidates (BM25 +45%-55% vs SPLADE++ ED +7%-20%)
results.quote: while reranking the top 100 BM25 candidates with RankZephyr results in a 45%–55% im- provement in effectiveness across various metrics, the improvement is more modest with SPLADE++ ED, ranging from 7%–20% for the same metrics.

results.claim: Teacher: GPT4 distillation on only 5K queries with ADA2 orderings was chosen; GPT4 data for 100K queries estimated over $10K
Stage 1 training took about 40 hours on eight A6000 GPUs

limits: Underperforms RankGPT4 out of domain (DL21, DL22, NEWS, COVID) when reranking SPLADE++ ED; authors say more work needed for a consistently better model
Authors suggest 4096 vs 8192 context and 2-4 points lower Judged@10 as plausible explanations
nDCG@10 for listwise runs is a lower bound because unjudged passages count as non-relevant (Judged@10 0.942 and 0.983 for DL19/DL20)
Teacher data limited to 5K GPT4 queries by cost
No latency, throughput or cost figures; English passage ranking only; NovelEval has only 21 queries
No separate Limitations section; no appendix
Stage-2 hyperparameters (lr, epochs, batch size) and optimizer not stated
